NEW_base64_carry_corruption_was_self_inf: CORRECTS THE 2026-11-24 DIAGNOSIS. Tonight's first base64 carry chunk returned a wrong md5 at an identical byte count - the exact 2026-11-24 symptom. Re-sending the SAME chunk produced the SAME wrong md5, so it was deterministic, not transport noise. Prefix bisection localised it to the first 250 bytes and a side-by-side dump showed it: container held ...2XLjRpemr..., Mac held ...2XLjRpamr... - one e became an a. The bridge did not do that. The payload had been retyped by hand out of one tool's output into another tool's argument and a character was mistyped. The 2026-11-24 'R written as an h' was the same thing. The lesson is NOT 'checksum harder' - it is NEVER RETYPE A PAYLOAD. Move bytes with a tool that takes a file path (device_commit_files). Keep the md5 check; it is what caught this.
